record.file_problem: This is repository metadata, README text, and a file list, not the contents of the result files. The README says the artifacts are from an earlier run and recommends rerunning the suite.
record.tranche_reason: The README says the repo re-tests difference-in-means refusal steering against SAE methods on Gemma-3-4B-IT, but describes a single-layer comparative suite rather than the original all-layer, all-position intervention.
record.gate_note: The README describes experiments and lists result files, but the results themselves are not available in the supplied text. It reports only that the earlier run's SAE arms were fully degenerate at coefficient 8 and that the decision rule returned pay_for_selectivity; it does not give claim-specific refusal or capability measurements for the difference-in-means arm. The reported degeneration is retained as an aggregate result, not treated as evidence about the direction.
record.test_reason: The repo's diff_in_means arm subtracts a difference-in-means refusal direction at layer 17 of Gemma-3-4B-IT and scores jailbreak rate, benign refusal and degeneracy, which bears on V1. The supplied text contains no results for that arm, so no verdict can be given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README gives the first run's verdict as pay_for_selectivity. It warns that this run used the 1,2,4,8 coefficient grid and pinned the one-coefficient experiments at 8, where SAE arms were degenerate, so three decision signals read noise. It also lacked capability and seed results. The authors advise rerunning before relying on any of it, and say the blog, docs and paper numbers describe that run.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a difference-in-means direction, but the described experiments steer at a selected layer (default 17) and compare it with SAE clamps and affine correction; the README does not describe the original all-layer, all-position ablation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says the earlier run used a coefficient grid of 1, 2, 4, 8 and pinned ablations at 8; the current described suite uses a swept coefficient grid and selects a coefficient for several experiments. No measured sensitivity outcomes are supplied.

fits_no_version.finding: In the first run, all SAE clamp arms were fully degenerate at coefficient 8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature clamping for refusal steering degrades output at high steering strength.

fits_no_version.finding: The first run's decision rule returned pay_for_selectivity. This implies per-category SAE features switched refusal off locally, which the README says one global direction cannot do. The README warns that the signals for experiments run at coefficient 8 were reading noise off broken arms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Category-specific SAE features allow refusal removal for one harm category alone, unlike a single global direction.

record.problems: The supplied README does not include the underlying results or separate arm-level measurements. It says the current artifacts come from an earlier run with an old coefficient grid, ablations pinned at 8, and no capability or seeds directory; it also warns that three decision signals were reading noise from broken arms.
record.rows_left_out: No numeric or arm-specific results from sweep, residual_leakage, cross_category, positions, adversarial, benchmark, or the other listed artifacts were supplied, so they could not be extracted. The README's pay_for_selectivity verdict is recorded in authors_conclusion but not as a measured outcome.

untested.parts: Addition of the direction to induce refusal is not described. Ablation across all layers and positions is not done; steering is at layer 17 only, with position variants. The diff-in-means arm's results are not in the supplied text.
No analysis of jailbreaks as direction suppression, and no adversarial training against ablation. The adversarial experiment tests harm detection under re-encoding, not attack mechanism.
The ACE (affine-correction) arm and the cross_category experiment are described, but no results are supplied.

missing.what: Jailbreak rate, benign refusal and degeneracy for the diff_in_means and ace arms across the coefficient grid
Cross-category refusal matrix (whether one category's feature or the global direction removes refusal selectively)
Position results (first token vs. all tokens vs. last prompt token) for the direction arm
MMLU and perplexity under direction steering. Not present in the first run; would come from a rerun.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README and file list were supplied. The study is not an original source. It uses diff-in-means as the baseline in an SAE-vs-linear comparison. Its diff-in-means results would bear on V1 (removal with capability cost), but none are present, so no labels are given.

versions.untested_parts: The README describes a difference-in-means steering arm, but does not provide its results. The described setup uses layer 17 rather than ablating the direction at every layer and position; it also does not report an addition result.
No weight edit or abliteration test is described.
No jailbreak attack that suppresses the direction, or training against its ablation, is described.
The README describes affine correction and a cross-category feature experiment, but gives no results establishing an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is described.
No language or model-variant transfer test is described.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is described.
